TreVeyon Henderson.note: Ruled out for the season opener after missing all game-week practices with the ankle injury suffered Aug. 24. Week 2 remains uncertain.

Zach Charbonnet.note: Unavailable for at least the first four games while rehabbing a torn ACL. Seattle has been encouraged by his rehab, but there is no firm return date.

Tory Horton.note: Was limited throughout game week and inactive for Seattle's opener. Hamstring issue follows an injury-interrupted 2025 season.

George Kittle.note: Successfully returned from the January Achilles tear in San Francisco's Week 1 win over the Rams, catching two of five targets for 12 yards with no reported in-game setback. His usage remained below a normal Kittle workload, but completing the game materially improves near-term availability confidence. Participation is expected to increase progressively in coming weeks.
George Kittle.expectedReturn: Active; workload expected to ramp up

Rome Odunze.status: Active Week 1 - calf; cleared through pregame testing
Rome Odunze.note: Odunze is officially active against Carolina after passing through pregame testing without a reported setback. That removes the remaining short-term availability uncertainty from his questionable designation. A modest workload cushion remains because he was limited in all three game-week practices while returning from the right calf strain.
Rome Odunze.expectedReturn: Active Week 1; modest workload limitation still possible

Jonathon Brooks.status: Cleared Week 1 - groin resolved; no limitations
Jonathon Brooks.note: Carolina removed Brooks from the final Week 1 injury report after he practiced fully Friday. Head coach Dave Canales said Brooks has no limitations entering the opener. The groin-related availability and workload penalties are removed; the residual long-term-risk modifier reflects his history of back-to-back right ACL surgeries rather than the resolved groin issue.

Zay Flowers.status: Day-to-day - aggravated left hamstring; MRI pending
Zay Flowers.note: Monday reporting from NFL Network says Flowers' hamstring aggravation is not considered serious and that he likely would have returned had Baltimore's opener been a playoff game. He remains set for an MRI and is considered day-to-day. That materially improves the near-term outlook from the prior severity-pending designation, but because this is a recurrence of the same hamstring issue that cost him practice time in late preseason, a moderate workload and reinjury-risk cushion remains until testing and Week 2 practice participation confirm his status.
Zay Flowers.expectedReturn: Week 2 possible; day-to-day pending MRI and practice participation

Michael Penix Jr..status: Inactive Week 1 - ACL return; targeting Week 2-3
Michael Penix Jr..note: Penix remains out for the opener while Atlanta completes his return-to-game ramp from the 2025 ACL tear, but Ian Rapoport now reports that he is specifically targeting Week 2 or Week 3 for his 2026 debut. That materially tightens and improves the prior open-ended timeline, so near-term availability is raised while the workload and residual post-ACL risk modifiers remain unchanged.

Tua Tagovailoa.note: Atlanta has ruled Tagovailoa out for the Week 1 opener after the oblique injury suffered during Thursday practice. He was absent from the media-access portion of Friday practice, and Cooper Rush will start against Pittsburgh. No firm return timetable beyond Week 1 has been announced, so Week 2 remains possible but uncertain.

Alvin Kamara.status: Expected OUT Week 1 - MCL; debut slated for Week 2
Alvin Kamara.note: Sunday-morning reporting from Nick Underhill says Kamara is not in line to play in the opener at Detroit and is instead slated to make his 2026 debut in Week 2 at Baltimore. That reverses the prior expectation that he would be active in a limited role. Availability is reduced for the confirmed near-term absence, while workload is raised modestly from the prior Week 1-limited assumption because the additional recovery week should improve his ramp when he returns.

Isiah Pacheco.note: On injured reserve and must miss at least four games. Detroit has not provided a firm return timetable.

Tank Dell.note: On injured reserve with a knee issue and unavailable until at least Week 5.

James Conner.note: On injured reserve with a foot injury and unavailable for the opening portion of the season.

Jeremiyah Love.status: Active Week 1 - high ankle sprain; reduced workload possible
Jeremiyah Love.note: Arizona officially made Love active against the Chargers, confirming his NFL debut after he returned to practice only last week following the high-ankle sprain. The prior final availability uncertainty is removed, but the workload penalty remains because of the recent injury and expected backfield split.

Josh Jacobs.note: Currently unavailable to play because of an off-field league status with no established football return date. This adjustment reflects availability uncertainty, not injury performance risk.

Brock Bowers.status: OUT Week 1 - meniscus trim; realistic Week 2 return chance
Brock Bowers.note: Bowers remains out for the opener after his meniscus trim, but ESPN reports the Raiders now believe there is a realistic chance he misses only one game and returns in Week 2 against the Chargers. That is a meaningful improvement from the prior one-to-two-game/Week 2-3 range. Availability is raised modestly while the expected early-return workload cushion and residual knee risk remain unchanged until he resumes practice.
Brock Bowers.expectedReturn: Week 2 possible; Raiders view one-game absence as realistic

Malik Nabers.note: Nabers is officially active for Sunday Night Football against Dallas after practicing fully throughout the week. That resolves the prior game-time availability uncertainty and materially improves his near-term outlook. A modest workload cushion remains because this is his first regular-season game back from ACL reconstruction with meniscus repair and a later follow-up procedure, and the Giants have not ruled out managing his snaps.
Malik Nabers.expectedReturn: Active Week 1; modest workload management still possible

Xavier Legette.note: Not listed on Carolina's Week 1 injury report after recovering from the August ankle injury and walking-boot period. He is medically cleared for the opener; any playing-time limitation is role-based rather than injury-based.

Jakobi Meyers.note: Jacksonville gave Meyers no final game designation after three limited practices with the thumb injury. He is cleared to play against Cleveland. A very small workload cushion remains because he practiced in a non-contact jersey earlier in the week and the injury involves his catching hand, but the prior availability concern is removed.

Marvin Mims Jr..status: Cleared Week 1 - foot; no game designation
Marvin Mims Jr..note: Denver's final Saturday injury report listed Mims as a full participant for the third straight practice and assigned him no game status. The Broncos said all 53 players are expected to be available Monday night against Kansas City, so the temporary workload cushion tied to the foot issue is removed.
Marvin Mims Jr..expectedReturn: Active Week 1; no injury limitation expected

Patrick Mahomes.note: Fully cleared following ACL/LCL rehabilitation and expected to start Week 1. Mahomes has reported no planned playing restrictions; only a minimal residual long-term post-reconstruction risk modifier remains until regular-season game action is confirmed.

A.J. Brown.status: IR - high-ankle sprain; approximately six-week absence expected
A.J. Brown.note: NFL Network's Ian Rapoport now reports Brown is expected to miss about six weeks with the right high-ankle sprain, a more specific and slightly longer outlook than the prior four-to-six-week range. New England has already placed him on injured reserve. The tighter six-week expectation lowers near-term availability and adds a modest return-to-workload and reinjury cushion.
A.J. Brown.expectedReturn: Approximately six weeks; likely Week 7-8 range

Sam Darnold.status: OUT multiple weeks - hip/glute injury; 4-6 week absence possible
Sam Darnold.note: New reporting from Pro Football Talk says Darnold could miss four to six weeks after the injury suffered in Seattle's opener. That is materially worse than the prior Week 2-out/Week 3-possible expectation. The injury is not considered season-ending and surgery is not expected, but the longer projected absence lowers near-term availability and adds a return-to-workload cushion.

Alec Pierce.status: Active Week 1 - heel/ankle surgery recovery; 20-30 snap count expected
Alec Pierce.note: NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reports Pierce is expected to play only about 20 to 30 snaps against Baltimore in Week 1. That is materially more restrictive than the prior generic managed-workload expectation and confirms a sharply reduced opening-week role while he completes his return from offseason lower-leg surgery. Availability remains full because he is expected to be active; the workload multiplier is reduced to reflect the concrete snap cap.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt.note: Washington says its full 53-man roster is medically cleared for Week 1, including Croskey-Merritt after he was limited Wednesday and Thursday with the groin injury. A modest workload cushion remains because the team indicated snap-count decisions could still be discussed for players returning from injuries, but he no longer carries a meaningful availability penalty.

De'Zhaun Stribling.status: OUT at least one month - left ankle deltoid sprain; surgery still possible
De'Zhaun Stribling.note: Stribling is expected to miss at least a month with a left-ankle deltoid sprain, and newer reporting says he is seeking additional medical opinions with surgery still possible even though it is not currently planned. That adds downside to both the return timeline and post-return workload/reinjury outlook versus the prior non-surgical assumption, so the availability, workload and long-term-risk multipliers are reduced modestly pending the final treatment decision.
De'Zhaun Stribling.expectedReturn: At least one month; approximately Week 6 or later, potentially longer if surgery is required

Sean Tucker.note: Tucker is officially inactive against Cincinnati after being listed doubtful throughout the weekend with the hamstring injury. Tampa Bay also elevated RB Josh Williams for additional backfield depth. The confirmed Week 1 absence removes the remaining chance that Tucker would dress in a limited role, so near-term availability is reduced while workload and long-term-risk assumptions for his eventual return remain unchanged.
Sean Tucker.expectedReturn: Week 2 possible; no firm return date

Jalen McMillan.note: McMillan is officially inactive against Cincinnati after carrying a doubtful designation because of the knee issue. His full Friday practice still supports a relatively short expected absence, but the confirmed Week 1 scratch removes the remaining possibility that he would be available for the opener and lowers near-term availability accordingly.
Jalen McMillan.expectedReturn: Week 2 possible; no firm return date

Dylan Sampson.status: Left-knee injury - postgame crutches/brace; further testing Monday
Dylan Sampson.note: Sampson was ruled out after injuring his left knee in Cleveland's opener, and postgame reporting now says he was on crutches with a brace on the knee. That materially raises concern versus the prior severity-pending designation even though no diagnosis has been announced. He is scheduled for further testing Monday, so the downgrade remains moderate rather than assuming a multi-week structural injury before imaging results are known.

Omar Cooper Jr..status: High-ankle sprain - ruled OUT Week 1; X-rays negative
Omar Cooper Jr..note: Follow-up reporting identifies Cooper's Week 1 ankle injury as a high-ankle sprain. X-rays were negative for a fracture, but the diagnosis materially increases concern for near-term availability compared with the prior severity-pending ankle designation. The Jets have not announced a firm return timetable, so availability and workload are reduced while the negative X-rays keep the long-term-risk adjustment modest.
Omar Cooper Jr..expectedReturn: Week 2 doubtful; return timetable not yet announced

Ja'Kobi Lane.status: Fractured wrist - expected to miss several weeks
Ja'Kobi Lane.note: NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport report that Lane fractured his wrist in Baltimore's Week 1 win and is expected to miss several weeks. Additional testing will determine the full extent of the injury. The confirmed fracture and multi-week absence materially worsen the prior severity-pending designation, so near-term availability, return-to-workload confidence and residual risk are reduced.

Kyler Murray.note: Murray remains in the NFL concussion protocol after the illegal hit that ended his Vikings debut, and Monday reporting citing Adam Schefter says he is not likely to play in Week 2 against Chicago. That materially lowers his near-term availability from the prior open Week 2 uncertainty. Because concussion clearance generally does not require a physical snap-count ramp once passed, workload remains close to normal for his eventual return while a small short-term recurrence/uncertainty cushion remains.
Kyler Murray.expectedReturn: Week 2 unlikely; Week 3 possible pending concussion-protocol clearance

Najee Harris.status: Healthy scratch Week 1 - Achilles medically cleared
Najee Harris.note: Updated reporting clarifies that Harris was not inactive because of the Achilles injury. He was a healthy scratch/coach's decision and was not listed on the Giants' injury report. The prior near-term availability and workload penalties are therefore removed. A small long-term-risk cushion remains because he is returning this season from the 2025 Achilles tear, but any Week 2 playing-time uncertainty is now treated as a depth-chart/role issue rather than an injury limitation.
Najee Harris.expectedReturn: Medically available Week 2; role/activation is coach's decision

Ladd McConkey.status: Left Week 1 - chest injury; severity pending
Ladd McConkey.note: McConkey left the Chargers' Week 1 loss to Arizona in the third quarter after a hard hit, was evaluated in the medical tent and then taken to the locker room. He was listed questionable to return and did not come back. Head coach Jim Harbaugh had no postgame update, so a temporary near-term availability and workload penalty is applied pending follow-up evaluation and Week 2 practice participation.
